tagline: A watch kept on the world — weather, markets, space weather, seismic and volcanic activity, satellites, and conflict, pulled live into one screen.
launchSub: Encrypted behind a login · public feeds only · runs entirely in your browser

cards.html: Vanilla JS pulling directly from public APIs — Open-Meteo, CoinGecko, Frankfurter, NOAA, USGS, NASA, weather.gov, wheretheis.at — no backend of its own, no data it collects. Everything renders client-side, in the browser running it.

features.d: current conditions and active NWS severe weather alerts.
NOAA SWPC solar activity, plus NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day.
USGS earthquake and volcanic activity, elevated-status alerts included.
live ISS position and satellite ground tracks.
a GDELT-driven monitor of active conflict activity worldwide.

lede: The information that actually matters day to day — is a storm coming, did the market move, is anything seismic or volcanic worth paying attention to, where's the ISS, what's happening globally — lives scattered across a dozen different sites and apps. Vigil is a single personal dashboard that pulls the live, public feeds worth checking into one place.
scope: This is a personal dashboard, not an early-warning system — treat every feed as informational, not authoritative, and go to the source (NWS, USGS, NOAA directly) for anything that actually matters in the moment. The dashboard itself is encrypted (AES-256, key derived from the operator name and access code) — without them the page is unreadable ciphertext, even in the source.
closing: A watch kept on the world, one feed at a time.
